description: issue #682 (slice I3): a handler block is NOT a procedure body, so `return`/`stop` inside it are `return`/`stop` OUTSIDE a procedure — even when the `when` was registered inside one. Here `when "start"` is registered inside `define setup`; the `"start"` handler fires immediately (the run has started) and hits `return 5`. Without a boundary conversion the `return` signal would escape into `setup`'s call frame and be silently consumed as `setup`'s own return; instead the handler boundary converts it to `ol-return-outside-proc` (spec/error-model.md), pointing at the `return` keyword. The escape is decided statically now, so the program does not run and no `return` trace event is emitted; under the `runUnchecked` opt-out the statement still emits one before the boundary reclassifies the escaping signal. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy does not appear beside the check's.
